finding: The current PID namespace used by os.getpid/killpg differs from the ancestor namespace exposed by mounted procfs. Accessing /proc/<syscall PID> or signalling a procfs-namespace PGID does not identify the intended process. The first affected batch had six passes, one failure and one error.
allowed_repair: Use /proc/self, PID-namespace inode and NSpid/NSpgid/NSsid to distinguish syscall namespace identities from ancestor procfs paths.
Apply that mapping consistently to owned-process discovery, parent route validation, environment/command-line reads, process-group signalling and observed process states.
Correct directly affected process_measurements group matching and wrapper RSS lookups; preserve their actual observation scope.
Preserve ambiguous or unobserved mappings as typed HOLD/warnings. Never signal unrelated namespaces or process groups.

preservation: Keep the first failed source/test bytes, first failed batch and diagnosis. Report new fixture before/after states as alive, zombie or gone when observed. The original failed fixture's state at failure remains NOT_OBSERVED.
